requirement_text.REQ-425:
MOB-6 in docs/mobile/requirements.md (build-order M6; depends on M2). Built BEFORE MOB-4 (REQ-426..428) -- see the S9 header: the renderers' six states classify this requirement's ApiError. SECURITY-REVIEWER gate (refresh-token handling, token clearing).

Hardens lib/api/api_client.dart (created by REQ-421) into the single client:
1. Attach the active tenant's bearer token (REQ-422's iss check).
2. On 401: exactly one silent refresh via flutter_appauth's token refresh, then exactly one retry of the original request; concurrent 401s share one in-flight refresh. On refresh failure: clear the tenant's tokens (REQ-422 store) and route to login.
3. Exponential backoff on 5xx for idempotent methods only (GET), bounded attempts; POST is not auto-retried (no duplicate task completion).
4. Normalise every failure to a sealed ApiError type before it leaves lib/api/: at minimum network-unavailable, unauthorized, forbidden (403), not-found, module-not-available (a 404 on any /api/v1/modules/<id>/ path -- architecture.md §6: absence is 404, not 403, and must not render as a generic not-found), backpressure (429, carrying the Retry-After seconds -- the backend emits 429 from lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex and lib/letflow/plugs/public_read_rate_limit.ex), validation (422 with RFC 9457 field errors), conflict (409), server (5xx after retries).
5. A static guard (apps/mobile/test/guards/), the counterpart of the SPA's raw-fetch-outside-client guard in web/tests/guards/: no file outside lib/api/ imports package:dio or package:http or uses dart:io HttpClient; with a self-test.

task.description:
Fresh full re-review of Step 2c after implementation rework 2 (handoffs/WF02-REQ425-20260929/step-02b-mobile-dev-rework2.json describes the fix: _bearerInterceptor now detects a retry re-dispatch via options.extra.containsKey(_kIssuedForRealmKey) and, on that path, re-verifies the tag against activeRealm.currentRealmUrl read fresh right there, immediately before attaching any token, rejecting with a _CrossTenantRetryAbortedException sentinel on mismatch so the request never reaches the transport layer). New regression test group 'cross-tenant retry-dispatch race (rework 2)' triggers the switch via a custom interceptor ahead of the bearer interceptor, landing it after refreshOnce() succeeds and the pre-fetch check passes but before the bearer interceptor's own re-check.

This is the third security review of this same file after two prior FAILs, both in the same defect class (cross-tenant token confusion around the refresh/retry sequence) but at different points in the sequence (token-write-time, then retry-dispatch-time). Read the CURRENT apps/mobile/lib/api/api_client.dart yourself -- do not trust the rework report. Specifically hunt for a THIRD window in the same sequence: is there any other point between 'the bearer interceptor's re-check passes' and 'the response is actually delivered to the original caller' where the active tenant could change again and the caller could receive/act on the wrong tenant's response (e.g. after a successful retry response arrives, is anything else read from activeRealm/tokenStore before the response reaches the caller)? Re-run the full INV-1..INV-8 procedure over the whole diff again, confirming all prior PASS verdicts still hold. If this is a genuine PASS, this closes REQ-425's security gate; if it FAILs for a fourth time in this same sequence, name that explicitly since rework budget would then be exhausted (rework_count would reach 3 of max_rework 3) and ORCH must escalate rather than dispatch further patches.
acceptance_criteria: a test where the fake server returns 401 once then 200 asserts exactly one refresh call and exactly one retry, and that two concurrent requests both receiving 401 trigger one refresh total
a test where refresh fails asserts the tenant's tokens are deleted from the secure store and the router is at the login route

a test asserts a GET receiving 503 twice then 200 succeeds with increasing delays between attempts (fake clock), a GET receiving 503 on every attempt stops after the maximum attempt count declared as a named constant in lib/api/ and surfaces ApiError server (the test asserts the exact number of requests sent), and a POST receiving 503 is not retried

a test per ApiError variant asserts the mapping from status code/exception, including 404 on /api/v1/modules/exam/x -> module-not-available, 404 elsewhere -> not-found, and 429 with 'Retry-After: 7' -> backpressure(7 seconds)
a test asserts no DioException or SocketException escapes lib/api/ -- the public client API returns or throws only ApiError
the single-client guard fails its self-test fixture (a file under lib/features/ importing package:dio) and passes on the real tree
cd apps/mobile && flutter analyze && flutter test pass, real output quoted, and SECURITY-REVIEWER signs off before merge

a regression test asserts the retry-dispatch window (post-refresh-success, pre-interceptor-chain) cannot serve a retried request under a tenant it was not issued for, distinct from the already-covered during-refresh window

result.summary:
Third full re-review, first-hand read of the CURRENT apps/mobile/lib/api/api_client.dart (823 lines) and its diff (api_client.dart, api_error.dart, auth.dart, navigation_bootstrap.dart, api.dart, plus tests). Hunted specifically for a fourth window strictly between '_bearerInterceptor's retry-dispatch re-check passes' and 'the response reaches the original caller' -- traced every read of activeRealm/tokenStore in the file: (1) _RefreshCoordinator._doRefresh (pre-network-call capture + post-network-call re-check before persisting, rework 1's fix, still intact); (2) ApiClient._handleUnauthorized's pre-fetch issuedForRealm-vs-current-realm check (still intact, though it no-ops when issuedForRealm is null -- see note below); (3) _bearerInterceptor's own token-attach-time re-check (rework 2's fix). After (3) passes and handler.next(options) runs, NOTHING in this file reads activeRealm or tokenStore again before the Response/ApiError reaches the caller -- _handleUnauthorized's post-retry handling (lines 593-609) branches purely on retryResponse.statusCode, and _sendWithBackoff/get/post pass the result straight through with no further tenant-scoped read. The token attached at (3) is read from a LOCAL realmUrl variable (never re-read from activeRealm after that point, including across the tokenStore.read await inside the interceptor), so even a tenant switch landing during that await cannot cause a mismatch between the tag and the token attached -- it only ever attaches the tag-tenant's own correct token, which is what makes the response inherently bound to the right tenant with no further re-verification needed downstream. No fourth window exists in this sequence. Noted (not a blocker, defense-in-depth already closes it): _handleUnauthorized's mid-level check (`issuedForRealm != null && issuedForRealm != activeRealm.currentRealmUrl`) short-circuits to no-op when issuedForRealm is legitimately null (request issued while no tenant was active); traced this edge case through _bearerInterceptor's own recheck on the retry pass (isRetryDispatch=true, issuedForRealm=null vs realmUrl=non-null after a tenant becomes active) and confirmed it still rejects via _CrossTenantRetryAbortedException -- the interceptor's independent recheck is why this isn't exploitable, not the mid-level check alone. Re-ran the full INV-1..INV-8 procedure over the whole diff (see per-invariant verdicts) -- all prior PASS/NOT-APPLICABLE verdicts hold. Ran `flutter analyze` (No issues found!) and `flutter test` (115 tests, all passed) myself, real output quoted below, not taken from the rework report. This closes REQ-425's security gate.

Scope test: apps/mobile/lib/api/api_client.dart, api_error.dart, apps/mobile/lib/auth/auth.dart (secret/token resolution and storage) and apps/mobile/lib/bootstrap/navigation_bootstrap.dart (activeRealm/token lifecycle around bootstrap/switch/logout) are all in scope -- this is a secret-resolving, token-handling, tenant-context-switching path.

INV-1 (tenant data isolation): APPLIES (this diff manages which tenant's bearer token/secrets are attached to a request, the client-side analogue of tenant scoping for this stage). SATISFIED -- token attach is keyed by realm_url (TenantTokenStore._keyFor), the retry-dispatch race (rework 2's specific target) and the original refresh-time race (rework 1) are both closed with regression tests (`cross-tenant refresh race (rework 1)`, `cross-tenant retry-dispatch race (rework 2)` groups in api_client_hardening_test.dart), both passing.
INV-2 (server-side field authorisation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no response field-shaping in this diff; ApiClient passes Response/ApiError through unmodified.
INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no Lua/WASM host function touched.
INV-4 (secrets by reference only): APPLIES (token/secret handling throughout). SATISFIED -- tokens resolved via TenantTokenStore (flutter_secure_storage) at point of use, never logged unredacted (RedactingLogInterceptor redacts Authorization headers and whole bodies on token-endpoint paths, token_redaction_test.dart passes), ApiError.NetworkUnavailableError.cause is a debug-only field never serialised into a response/log payload beyond local toString. Grep of config/lib for hardcoded secrets not applicable to this Dart diff; no new secret-resolution code outside the established TenantTokenStore/AppAuthAdapter pattern.
INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability): NOT-APPLICABLE -- client-side error classification (api_error.dart), not a server lookup-by-ID path; module-not-available vs not-found distinction here is the REQ-425 requirement text's own explicit design (architecture.md §6), not a violation of server-side 404/403 collapsing.
INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping): APPLIES -- this handoff itself is the proof; SECURITY-REVIEWER handoff exists, PASS, with per-invariant verdicts recorded here.
INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no SQL in this diff.
INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths): APPLIES (network/transport-input-handling code). SATISFIED -- classifyError/_parseFieldErrors/_parseRetryAfter all total functions with explicit fallback branches on malformed input, no bare `{:ok, x} =`-equivalent unguarded pattern match on external I/O; DioException is always caught and reclassified, never left to propagate (test: 'no raw transport exception escapes lib/api/ (AC5)', passing).

`flutter analyze` output: 'Analyzing mobile... No issues found! (ran in 5.3s)'.
`flutter test` output (apps/mobile): 115 examples, 'All tests passed!' -- includes both cross-tenant race regression groups, the new retry-dispatch-race group, guard self-tests (single_api_client_guard_test.dart), and all pre-existing suites (bootstrap, auth, security, widgets) with no regressions.
result.next_action: Route to REVIEWER (Step 2d/OTP-idiom-and-scope gate) -- REQ-425's security gate is now closed; no further security rework needed.

gate_history.summary: INV-1 BLOCKER: _RefreshCoordinator._doRefresh captured realmUrl before awaiting the refresh network call, allowing a concurrent tenant switch/logout to resurrect old-tenant tokens and cause a silent cross-tenant retry.
issues: _RefreshCoordinator._doRefresh/_handleUnauthorized do not re-verify the active tenant/clientId is unchanged after the async refresh completes -- untested cross-tenant race
gate_history.next_action: Route back to MOBILE-DEV (rework) to add a realm/clientId re-check before persisting refreshed tokens and before reissuing the retry, plus a regression test.

gate_history.summary: Related but distinct INV-1 BLOCKER: rework1 correctly closed the race inside _doRefresh, but the bearer interceptor's fresh unguarded read of activeRealm at retry-dispatch time (a real dio 5.11.1 event-loop turn) reopens the same defect class one step later.
issues: _handleUnauthorized's pre-fetch check does not survive into _bearerInterceptor's own later, independent realm read -- retry can be dispatched with the new tenant's token
gate_history.next_action: Route back to MOBILE-DEV for rework 2: close the retry-dispatch-time realm race in _handleUnauthorized/_bearerInterceptor, with a regression test covering the post-refresh-success, pre-retry-dispatch window specifically.
